works/origen-de-principiis/summary: The first Christian systematic theology: God, the Logos, the Spirit, rational creatures, free will, restoration, and the interpretation of Scripture.
works/origen-de-principiis/significance: Source of the eternal generation of the Son, of three hypostases, and of later controversies over apokatastasis.
works/arius-letter-to-eusebius/summary: Arius complains of persecution by Bishop Alexander and summarises his teaching that the Son has a beginning and was made from nothing. Preserved by Theodoret (Ecclesiastical History 1.4) and Epiphanius.
works/arius-letter-to-eusebius/significa: One of the few surviving texts by Arius himself.
works/athanasius-on-the-incarnation/titl: On the Incarnation of the Word (De Incarnatione)
works/athanasius-on-the-incarnation/summ: Why the Word became flesh: to restore the image of God in fallen humanity, defeat death and corruption, and reveal the Father. Dated variously c. 318 or c. 335.
works/athanasius-on-the-incarnation/sign: Classic statement of incarnation and deification; its soteriology underlies the Nicene case against Arius.
works/athanasius-against-the-arians/titl: Discourses Against the Arians (Orationes contra Arianos)
works/athanasius-against-the-arians/summ: Athanasius' main anti-Arian work: a refutation of Arius' Thalia and an exegesis of contested texts such as Proverbs 8:22, Philippians 2:9 and Hebrews 3:2.
works/athanasius-against-the-arians/sign: Set the exegetical terms of Nicene theology, including the principle of reading texts of lowliness as referring to the incarnate Son.
works/basil-letters/summary: Over 360 letters, including Letter 236 and Letter 38 (sometimes attributed to Gregory of Nyssa) on the distinction of ousia and hypostasis.
works/basil-letters/significance: Primary source for the Cappadocian distinction between common essence and particular persons.
works/gregory-theological-orations/summa: Five sermons preached in Constantinople defending the Trinity against the Eunomians and the deity of the Spirit against the Pneumatomachians.
works/gregory-theological-orations/signi: Earned Gregory the title ‘the Theologian’; a classic of Trinitarian theology.
works/gregory-oration-40/summary: Gregory's Epiphany sermon on baptism, ending with an exposition of the Trinity confessed at baptism.
works/gregory-oration-40/significance: Contains his celebrated description of contemplating the One and the Three.
works/gregory-nyssa-to-ablabius/title: To Ablabius: That There Are Not Three Gods
works/gregory-nyssa-to-ablabius/summary: Gregory answers the charge that three persons sharing one nature are three gods, arguing from the unity of divine activity.
works/gregory-nyssa-to-ablabius/signific: A key text on inseparable operations and the unity of the Trinity.
works/jerome-against-luciferians/summary: A dialogue arguing that bishops who signed the Homoian creed of Ariminum (359) under pressure should be received back, against the rigorist followers of Lucifer of Cagliari.
works/jerome-against-luciferians/signifi: Contains Jerome's famous description of the Arian ascendancy in 359.
works/augustine-de-trinitate/summary: Fifteen books (c. 400–420): the scriptural basis of the Trinity, the logic of relations, and analogies of the Trinity in the human mind (memory, understanding, will).
works/augustine-de-trinitate/significanc: The most influential Western work on the Trinity; basis of the Filioque and of scholastic Trinitarianism.
works/photius-mystagogy/summary: Photius' systematic case against the Filioque: biblical, patristic and logical arguments that the Spirit proceeds from the Father alone.
works/photius-mystagogy/significance: The classic Byzantine statement against the Filioque.
works/racovian-catechism/summary: The confession of the Minor Reformed Church of Poland, published at Raków: one God the Father, Jesus a man raised to divine authority, rejection of satisfaction atonement.
works/racovian-catechism/significance: The classic statement of Socinian antitrinitarianism, influential in Dutch and English rationalism.
works/channing-unitarian-christianity/su: Channing's ordination sermon for Jared Sparks in Baltimore, setting out rational interpretation of Scripture, the unity of God, the unity of Christ and the moral perfection of God.
works/whitehead-process-and-reality/summ: Whitehead's Gifford Lectures (1927–28) presenting a metaphysics of actual occasions and a dipolar God.
works/whitehead-process-and-reality/sign: Foundational text of process philosophy and theology.
works/didache/title: Didache (The Teaching of the Twelve Apostles)
works/didache/summary: Short church manual with the "Two Ways" moral teaching, instructions on baptism, fasting, the Lord’s Prayer, eucharistic thanksgivings (chs. 9–10), Sunday assembly (ch. 14) and itinerant prophets.
works/didache/significance: Earliest surviving church order, rediscovered in 1873 (published 1883); key evidence for Jewish-rooted early Christian worship and ethics.
works/apostolic-tradition/summary: Church order containing ordination rites, an early eucharistic prayer and the baptismal rite with triple interrogation.
works/apostolic-tradition/significance: Its anaphora became the basis of Eucharistic Prayer II of the 1970 Roman Missal; its date, origin and attribution to Hippolytus are debated.
works/divine-liturgy-chrysostom/title: Divine Liturgy of St John Chrysostom
works/divine-liturgy-chrysostom/summary: The ordinary eucharistic liturgy of the Byzantine rite, with its anaphora traditionally attributed to John Chrysostom, celebrated in Greek, Slavonic, Arabic, Romanian, Georgian, English and many other languages.
works/divine-liturgy-chrysostom/signific: The most widely used Eastern liturgy, the central act of worship of Eastern Orthodox and Byzantine Catholic churches.
works/luther-deutsche-messe/title: German Mass and Order of Service (Deutsche Messe)
works/luther-deutsche-messe/summary: Vernacular evangelical order of the Mass with chorales, preaching and communion.
works/luther-deutsche-messe/significance: Model for Lutheran church orders and congregational singing.
works/book-of-common-prayer/summary: Cranmer’s English liturgy for daily offices, Holy Communion, baptism, marriage, burial and ordination; standard revision of 1662.
works/book-of-common-prayer/significance: Shaped Anglican worship worldwide and the English language itself.
works/barclay-apology/title: An Apology for the True Christian Divinity
works/barclay-apology/summary: Fifteen propositions defending Quaker doctrine, including inward revelation, silent worship and spiritual sacraments.
works/barclay-apology/significance: The standard Quaker theology for two centuries.
works/watts-hymns-spiritual-songs/summar: Collection of some 200 freely composed hymns for congregational singing.
works/watts-hymns-spiritual-songs/signif: Launched the English hymn tradition beyond metrical psalmody.
works/finney-lectures-on-revivals/summar: Finney’s lectures arguing that revivals result from the right use of means, and defending "new measures" such as the anxious bench and protracted meetings.
works/finney-lectures-on-revivals/signif: Handbook of American revivalism and of pragmatic, results-oriented worship.
works/nevin-anxious-bench/summary: Critique of revivalist techniques in favour of catechetical, churchly piety.
works/nevin-anxious-bench/significance: Classic objection to revivalism from within the Reformed tradition.
works/sacrosanctum-concilium/title: Sacrosanctum Concilium (Constitution on the Sacred Liturgy)
works/sacrosanctum-concilium/summary: Vatican II’s charter for liturgical reform.
works/sacrosanctum-concilium/significanc: Basis of the post-conciliar reform of all Catholic rites.
works/traditionis-custodes/summary: Motu proprio restricting celebration of the pre-1970 Roman Missal.
works/traditionis-custodes/significance: Reversed Summorum Pontificum and reopened the "liturgy wars".
